title: Learning Without Forgetting for Vision-Language Models
authors: Da-Wei Zhou, Yuanhan Zhang, Yan Wang, Jingyi Ning, Han-Jia Ye, De-Chuan Zhan, Ziwei Liu
lab: LAMDA Group, Nanjing University (with Nanyang Technological University)
one_line: Grows one task-specific projection per incremental task on frozen CLIP encoders and fuses visual with textual features, so old tasks survive by module expansion rather than replay.
contribution: Keeps CLIP's image and text encoders frozen and, for every new task, expands a fresh task-specific projection while fixing all previous ones, so adaptation happens in added capacity instead of overwriting old parameters. A fusion module jointly adjusts visual and textual features before classification, recovering cross-modal task semantics that uni-modal CIL pipelines discard. Memory grows linearly with tasks but each unit is projection-only, making the stability/plasticity trade-off explicit rather than a regularization penalty.
why_it_matters: The most cited (56+) 2025 statement of the projection-expansion recipe for VLM-based CIL; it is the baseline that later CLIP-CIL prompt, adapter and knowledge-injection work (e.g. ENGINE) positions against.
key_result: n/a - reports SOTA across nine continual-learning benchmark datasets and multiple VLM backbones; no single headline delta in the abstract.

title: External Knowledge Injection for CLIP-Based Class-Incremental Learning
authors: Da-Wei Zhou, Kai-Wen Li, Jingyi Ning, Han-Jia Ye, Lijun Zhang, De-Chuan Zhan
one_line: Reinjects the fine-grained visual and textual context that incremental CLIP training overwrites, using augmented visual branches plus GPT-4-rewritten class descriptors and inference-time re-ranking.
contribution: Argues that CLIP-CIL collapses to coarse class-name matching and loses contextual attributes, and that continual updates erase whatever fine-grained description remains. ENGINE adds a dual-branch injection tuning framework: a visual branch enriched by data augmentation and a textual branch where GPT-4 rewrites discriminative descriptors into class-context knowledge, so detail is supplied from outside the model instead of being recovered inside it. Post-tuning knowledge is then applied as an inference-time re-ranking step as the data stream evolves. Code: github.com/LAMDA-CL/ICCV25-ENGINE.
why_it_matters: Marks the 2025 shift from 'protect CLIP from forgetting' to 'feed CLIP external knowledge': the remedy becomes text-side and inference-time, which reframes CLIP-CIL as a knowledge-supply problem rather than a weight-protection problem.
key_result: n/a - claims state-of-the-art CLIP-based CIL results; abstract reports no single number.

title: CL-MoE: Enhancing Multimodal Large Language Model with Dual Momentum Mixture-of-Experts for Continual Visual Question Answering
authors: Tianyu Huai, Jie Zhou, Xingjiao Wu, Qin Chen, Qingchun Bai, Ze Zhou, Liang He
lab: School of Computer Science and Technology, East China Normal University
one_line: Routes LoRA experts inside an MLLM with task-level and instance-level routers plus momentum expert updates, so continual VQA adds capacity without overwriting the backbone's commonsense knowledge.
contribution: Inserts a Dual-Router MoE into an MLLM: a task-level router selects global experts and an instance-level router selects local experts, so different VQA tasks activate different weight subsets while the shared MLLM knowledge stays intact. A dynamic Momentum MoE updates expert parameters according to expert-task/instance relations instead of uniformly fine-tuning, absorbing new VQA knowledge with reduced interference. Evaluated on a 10-task continual VQA sequence.
why_it_matters: An early CVPR-level demonstration that MoE adapters, not prompts or replay, are the natural continual-learning interface for MLLMs - the line that 2026 structured-expert work (Monarch-MoE) pushes toward gradient-level isolation.
key_result: State of the art across 10 VQA tasks (no aggregate numeric delta in abstract).

title: SMoLoRA: Exploring and Defying Dual Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Visual Instruction Tuning
authors: Ziqi Wang, Chang Che, Qi Wang, Yangyang Li, Zenglin Shi, Meng Wang
lab: Hefei University of Technology (with Tsinghua University and Academy of Cyber)
one_line: Names 'dual' catastrophic forgetting in MLLM instruction tuning - lost visual understanding plus degraded instruction following - and separates the two with dual-routed low-rank experts.
contribution: Shows that continual visual instruction tuning degrades two distinct capabilities: previously learned visual understanding and the model's instruction-following behaviour, a dual forgetting that single-objective CL methods miss. SMoLoRA uses a Separable Mixture of Low-Rank Adaptation with two routing modules, one specializing visual understanding and one instruction following, so learning a new task does not consume the routing capacity needed by the other. It also introduces a CVIT benchmark that additionally measures generalization to unseen tasks and robustness to diverse instruction phrasings.
why_it_matters: Reframes MLLM continual learning as capability-level forgetting rather than class-level forgetting, and its benchmark moves CL evaluation to unseen-task transfer and instruction robustness - the two properties MLLM users actually care about.
key_result: n/a - abstract reports gains on dual-forgetting, unseen-task generalization and instruction robustness without a single aggregate number; benchmark at github.com/Minato-Zackie/SMoLoRA.

title: LoRA Subtraction for Drift-Resistant Space in Exemplar-Free Continual Learning
one_line: Subtracts old tasks' LoRA weights from the pre-trained weights before each new task, constructing a drift-resistant feature space without storing exemplars or old-task statistics.
contribution: Targets feature drift in exemplar-free CL without exemplars or stale statistics: before learning a task, it subtracts the LoRA deltas accumulated on previous tasks from the frozen pre-trained weight to build a Drift-Resistant Space (DRS), then trains the new task's LoRA inside that space. Because the correction is parameter-space arithmetic rather than stored features, it tracks how the feature space actually evolves instead of relying on static snapshots. Stabilizing the space then permits a triplet loss, so the method buys plasticity rather than trading it away.
why_it_matters: A cheap, deployment-friendly 2025 answer to exemplar-free CL that reuses the LoRA parameterization for both adaptation and drift correction - the same task-vector-arithmetic intuition now spreading into merging-based CL.
key_result: n/a - consistent SOTA across multiple datasets with gains growing on long task sequences; no single number in abstract.

title: Synthetic Data is an Elegant GIFT for Continual Vision-Language Models
authors: Bin Wu, Wuxuan Shi, Jinqiao Wang, Mang Ye
lab: School of Computer Science, Wuhan University (with CAS Institute of Automation)
one_line: Regenerates pre-training and past-task image-text pairs with a text-to-image diffusion model, then distills on the synthetic pairs so a continually fine-tuned VLM keeps both task and pre-training knowledge.
contribution: Observes that continual VLM fine-tuning corrupts downstream-task knowledge and the original pre-training distribution, while the pre-training data itself is unavailable. GIFT uses a pre-trained text-to-image diffusion model to recreate both pre-training and previously learned task data, then applies a contrastive distillation loss with an image-text alignment constraint on the synthetic pairs so replayed knowledge is preserved in the VLM's feature space. Adaptive weight consolidation with Fisher information computed from the synthetic pairs balances stability and plasticity when generated data is scarce.
why_it_matters: Synthetic generative replay is the 2025 answer to the no-data, no-exemplar constraint for VLMs; it connects diffusion models to continual learning as a data source rather than only as the object being trained.
key_result: n/a - consistently outperforms prior SOTA across settings per abstract; no single number reported.

title: One-for-More: Continual Diffusion Model for Anomaly Detection
authors: Xiaofan Li, Xin Tan, Zhuo Chen, Zhizhong Zhang, Ruixin Zhang, Rizen Guo, Guannan Jiang, Yulong Chen, Yanyun Qu, Lizhuang Ma, Yuan Xie
lab: East China Normal University (with Tencent YouTu/WeChatPay, CATL, Xiamen University, SJTU)
topic: continual anomaly detection with diffusion models
one_line: Makes a diffusion-based anomaly detector continual via gradient projection, with an iterative SVD trick that avoids storing Markov-chain activations, plus anomaly-masked conditioning.
contribution: Identifies 'faithfulness hallucination' and catastrophic forgetting when a diffusion anomaly detector meets new normal-pattern increments, and applies gradient projection so updates are biased toward directions that preserve learned knowledge. Because projection for diffusion would otherwise require storing activations across the whole Markov process, it derives an iterative SVD method from the transitivity of linear representations, cutting memory to a tiny footprint with almost no performance loss. An anomaly-masked network strengthens the diffusion conditioning mechanism to reduce over-fitting to normal images.
why_it_matters: Shows continual learning can be imposed on generative detectors, not only discriminative classifiers; the gradient-projection-plus-SVD recipe is a template for CL in diffusion models where activation storage is prohibitive.
key_result: First place in 17 of 18 continual anomaly-detection settings (per abstract).

title: MuseumMaker: Continual Style Customization Without Catastrophic Forgetting
authors: Chenxi Liu, Gan Sun, Wenqi Liang, Jiahua Dong, Can Qin, Yang Cong
lab: State Key Laboratory of Robotics, Shenyang Institute of Automation, CAS (with UCAS and SCUT)
chinese_institution: Chinese Academy of Sciences (Shenyang Institute of Automation) / UCAS
one_line: Learns a shared LoRA for text-to-image customization, regularized by style distillation plus weight/feature regularization so each new user style does not erase earlier ones.
contribution: Formulates continual style customization for text-to-image diffusion: each new user style arrives as a few-shot set and must be learned without forgetting earlier styles. A style distillation loss extracts style from the new few-shot images while minimizing bias from their content, attacking catastrophic overfitting; a dual regularization on a shared-LoRA module constrains updates in both weight and feature space; and a task-wise token embedding gives every style a dedicated representational anchor to compensate for LoRA's limited capacity.
why_it_matters: Extends continual learning from recognition to generative personalization, where forgetting is a product failure (a user's earlier styles degrade); one of the earliest TIP-level treatments of continual LoRA for diffusion.
key_result: n/a - validated on diverse style datasets for robustness and style fidelity; abstract reports no aggregate number.

title: Continual Instruction Tuning for Large Multimodal Models
authors: Jinghan He, Haiyun Guo, Kuan Zhu, Ming Tang, Jinqiao Wang
lab: Foundation Model Research Center, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (with UCAS)
chinese_institution: Chinese Academy of Sciences (Institute of Automation)
one_line: Builds the first benchmark for continual instruction tuning of LMMs, shows catastrophic forgetting is real there, and adds task-similarity-informed regularization and model expansion.
contribution: Asks two controlled questions - whether LMMs forget under continual instruction tuning, and whether image-classification CL methods transfer - and answers them with a new benchmark that reveals clear catastrophic forgetting. It then adapts replay, regularization and expansion strategies to the instruction-tuning setting and quantifies task-similarity dynamics between pairs of vision-language tasks. Finally it proposes task-similarity-informed regularization and model expansion, which consistently improve performance.
why_it_matters: The evaluation substrate for Chinese continual visual instruction tuning (SMoLoRA and later MLLM continual-tuning papers benchmark against it): it turns 'does forgetting happen?' into a measurable protocol for LMMs.
key_result: n/a - quantitative study; its task-similarity-informed regularization and expansion consistently boost performance without a single headline number in the abstract.

title: Merge then Realign: Simple and Effective Modality-Incremental Continual Learning for Multimodal LLMs
authors: Dingkun Zhang, Shuhan Qi, Xinyu Xiao, Kehai Chen, Xuan Wang
one_line: Explains modality-incremental MLLM degradation as forgetting plus modality-agnostic/modality-specific misalignment, and fixes both by merging the new modality branch then re-aligning.
contribution: Diagnoses modality-incremental continual learning (MCL) for MLLMs as two coupled failures: conventional forgetting, and misalignment between modality-agnostic and modality-specific components once a new encoder is added. MERA merges the newly trained modality branch into the existing MLLM and then re-aligns the merged model, without adding heavy parameters or changing the architecture, which keeps it reusable across MLLM families. Evaluated by extending an MLLM to four modalities.
why_it_matters: The cheapest known route to near-lossless modality addition (99.84% backward relative gain): it argues that for MLLMs the right CL primitive may be weight merging plus realignment rather than replay or prompt banks.
key_result: 99.84% average Backward Relative Gain when extending to four modalities (near-lossless modality-incremental CL).

title: Monarch-MoE: Structured Experts for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
authors: Xi Zhang, Boyu Diao, Zesen Chen, Ruiqi Liu, Hangda Liu, Yongjun Xu
lab: Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences (with UCAS and ShanghaiTech)
chinese_institution: Chinese Academy of Sciences (Institute of Computing Technology)
topic: multimodal continual instruction tuning / structured MoE-LoRA
one_line: Replaces dense LoRA expert factors with block-diagonal Monarch factors so each block-pair update touches only one output block, giving blockwise gradient isolation at roughly half the adapter parameters.
contribution: Observes that even multi-expert LoRA fails to isolate updates because a dense low-rank expert's update spreads over many output features. Monarch-MoE substitutes block-diagonal factors connected by a fixed permutation for the dense LoRA factors, so a block-pair update affects exactly one output block while connections between all input and output blocks are preserved. Batched computation, fused forward operators and an optimized backward pass make the compact experts trainable on a single 24 GB RTX 4090.
why_it_matters: Pushes the MoE-LoRA line (CL-MoE, MoE-Adapters) from routing-level isolation to parameter-level gradient isolation, and targets the hardware budget that actually blocks MLLM continual tuning in academic labs.
key_result: First-task forgetting as low as 0.52 percentage points on MLLM-DCL and 0.10 on UCIT with LLaVA-1.5-7B, with about 75% and 50% fewer adapter parameters, respectively; single 24 GB RTX 4090.

title: EmbodiedCLBench: Evaluating Continual Learning for Self-Evolving Embodied Agents
authors: Jie Huang, Yanan Chen, Ruixun Liu, Kaichen He, Xinyi He, Rui Huang, Zilong Zheng, Zhenliang Zhang, Yiwu Zhong
lab: School of Intelligence Science and Technology, Peking University, and BIGAI
chinese_institution: Peking University / Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence (BIGAI)
one_line: First embodied-simulation benchmark for continual learning of self-evolving agents, scoring whether basic-task experience can be recomposed to solve unseen advanced tasks.
contribution: Argues that CL research remains confined to non-embodied settings and builds EmbodiedCLBench in embodied simulation with compositional generalization as the core principle: agents first learn basic tasks, then must recombine the acquired skills to solve complex unseen tasks. It evaluates multiple agent harnesses and learning methods, and reports that experience from basic tasks gives consistent improvement that stays stable as task complexity rises, but does not scale with the number of learning samples.
why_it_matters: Moves the CL frontier from static image streams to interactive embodied agents and delivers a direct negative result for 'self-evolving agent' claims: current agents cannot extract information from additional experience.
key_result: Negative scaling: gains from basic-task experience are stable under rising complexity but do not grow with more learning samples; advanced tasks are largely unsolvable zero-shot (per abstract).

title: PaLoRA: Paced Low-Rank Adaptation for Continual Learning
authors: Yuxuan Li, Fanhu Zeng, Hao Tang
lab: Peking University (with CAS Institute of Automation)
chinese_institution: Peking University / Chinese Academy of Sciences (Institute of Automation)
topic: LoRA continual learning / theory of plasticity control
one_line: Derives a pacing law s* = sqrt(R/c) for how strongly to restrict LoRA gradient steps as the effective rank R of past knowledge grows, and implements it with SVD truncation plus null-space projection.
contribution: Shows that even under directional constraints such as null-space projection, finite-precision updates inevitably leak into the subspace of prior knowledge along multiple directions, and that a fixed small learning rate only attenuates leakage - accumulated forgetting still grows with the effective rank of historical knowledge. Under an anisotropic leakage model it derives the optimal magnitude restriction s* = sqrt(R/c), which increases with effective rank to balance stability and plasticity. PaLoRA implements the law with adaptive SVD truncation of historical knowledge, null-space projection of gradients and rank-aware adaptive pacing.
why_it_matters: Turns the ubiquitous 'use a small learning rate' heuristic in LoRA-based continual learning into a principled, rank-dependent schedule - one of the few theory-to-method transfers on the PEFT side in 2025-26, aimed at the long-horizon sequences where heuristics break.
key_result: +4% accuracy on 50-task ImageNet-A and ImageNet-R sequences over prior methods (per abstract).

title: RIFAR: Reliability and Forgetting-Aware Replay for Continual Robot Learning
authors: Zirui Song, Zheng Lu, Haoran Liao, Wanqi Zhong, Yunhe Ni, Lijie Wang, Xiuying Chen
lab: Tsinghua University and Zhejiang University (with MBZUAI)
one_line: Reconstructs robot experience with a world-action model, screens trajectories with a frozen inverse-dynamics model for action-visual consistency, and replay-selects by measured policy drift.
contribution: Replaces stored demonstrations with a world-action model that regenerates past experience from compact demonstration prefixes, then gates what is replayed: a frozen inverse-dynamics model scores action-visual consistency to filter visually coherent but physically unrealizable rollouts. Training mixes current demonstrations with the highest-quality screened trajectories, then compares action predictions before and after adaptation on identical historical inputs and re-selects trajectories with larger normalized drift for continued training. Evaluated on three LIBERO suites and real-world experiments.
why_it_matters: Attacks the two failure modes of generative replay for embodied policies - hallucinated actions and forgetting caused by adaptation itself - and cuts replay storage from full demonstrations to a few percent.
key_result: 90.97 AUC on LIBERO-Goal while retaining about 320 historical time steps per task (roughly 4.9% of the steps used by 50-demonstration replay); SOTA over prior WAM-based generative replay across three LIBERO suites plus real-world experiments.
